items.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: We started studying with Trungpa Rinpoche at Naropa Institute in Boulder, Colorado.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, it’s a big part of it. A big part of it is you go back to being alive, which means breathe. My voice workshop is breathe in, breathe out, inhale, exhale. It’s the only way we are in the moment. Stuff comes up in our mind, you see it, you don’t get involved, you let it go and you go back to just breathe in, breathe out. Be totally in the moment. And the moment, the second you express yourself creatively and it comes from a total open place, that’s the state of enlightenment. That would be the state of…

so absolutely beautiful. And he was on heroin all day long you know. You still have these glimpses of being totally in the moment and totally identified with the music and with what you do. Oh that’s a big thing, together with it comes that we are both studying Buddhism. You know we have a big monastery here. We started studying with Trungpa Rinpoche at Naropa Institute in Boulder, Colorado. And it simply had to do with — we came over here and my father died. And I’m probably one of the more lucky ones.
